items.text: Arm, in the Form's Clock row. It shows the timeline ("armed · tap to start") without running the clock. The first tap on the timeline starts it; Start, Pause and Reset also clear Arm.
A flyout stays anchored to its button: it hangs down from the button's top when it fits, otherwise it rises from the button's bottom, and it follows the button if the window changes.
The first and last picture in a flyout round with its yellow edge, so the top left corner is round too.
A hold-flyout has a bright yellow edge, so it reads as open.
Hold-flyouts are a mirror of the rail: flush against the button's left edge, straight right edge, square dividers, rounded left corners, starting at the button's height and running down.
The yellow mark on the active rail button is a 2 px line right on the pill's edge.
The A|B slider's pull toward the middle is soft: it slows as you come close and settles on 50% when you hover there, instead of snapping.
The metronome's disc now sits behind the wave line and the A|B line, and only its picture floats in front of everything.
The A|B slider's end triangles join its line as one shape.
The A|B slider's end marks are small triangles pointing in, and the B label no longer covers one.
